rationales.react.maxComponentComplexity: Synthetic bench fixture: the components are deliberately tiny, so the complexity threshold is lowered from the default 20 to 10 to exercise the complexity rule without a 20-branch example. Test-only; does not reflect production guidance.

description: React component analysis: 7 rules across 10 files, 25 expected violations. Complexity 12 triggers severe + no-error-boundary + performance (memoization). AsyncWidget has useEffect → no-error-boundary. Dashboard calls fetchUserData (no 'use' prefix) → hooks-naming. AlertBanner uses non-destructured props → missing-props. HeavyRenderer memo + missing-keys → performance ×2. PhotoGallery (no alt) + ModalToggle (div onClick) → accessibility ×2. ModalToggle inline onClick → performance (legitimate FP, added v3.4.8). App-level no-error-boundary (13 components, 0 boundaries) → no-error-boundary (legitimate FP, added v3.4.8). raw-element: 4 raw <button> usages across LoginForm, SignupForm, DeleteButton, NavBar — exported Button wrapper auto-detected, minUsages=5 satisfied. Also 2 collateral raw-element from existing accessibility.tsx:39 and performance.tsx:23 (now enabled by rawElementCheck). raw-element.tsx collateral: missing-props ×4 (all non-PropTypes components), performance ×2 (Button inline fn params + DeleteButton inline onClick), accessibility (DeleteButton div onClick). Near-miss: good-hook.tsx (well below complexity, no hooks), raw-element-near-miss.tsx (uses React.createElement with Button wrapper → no JSX nodes, no violations).
